transcript:
Header:
2025-02-28 16:00 UTC · Duration: 38 minutes · Attendees: Lena Morales (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Redwood Product), Mark Davenport (Aurora CTO), Priya Singh (Aurora Platform), Janelle Ortiz (Aurora Security), Evan Ross (Aurora DevOps)

Summary: Quick product walkthrough focused on rate limits, org vs project keys, quotas, multi-tenant controls for Aurora's multi-product healthcare platform. Customer wants predictable token budgets per product, strict per-project throttles during spikes, and clear audit trails for compliance.

00:00 Lena: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll keep this short, Samir and i will run through how redwood does rate limits, org and project keys, and some of the console flows. 
00:10 Mark: yep, thanks lena, we've got about 35 minutes, want to understand how we can map our products to projects, and how to guarantee budgets without breaking latency SLAs.
00:22 Samir: great, quick agenda: 1) key types and scoping, 2) quota vs rate limit difference, 3) console demo of policies, 4) failover/fallback behaviors, 5) q&a.
00:35 Priya: quick note, our regulatory team will want audit logs and KMS integration, janelle is here and can chime in.
00:42 Janelle: yes security will want to see retention windows and access controls, also SSO and RBAC.
00:49 Samir: all covered, we'll show where that lives. starting with keys — we have org keys that sit at the account level, and project keys that you can issue per product or environment. org keys can be used for admin ops and broad access, project keys are scoped to quotas and routes.
01:10 Mark: so we could give each of our products a project key and set a token budget per month?
01:16 Lena: exactly, you can set both rate limits (requests/sec or tokens/sec) and monthly quotas (total tokens) per project key. you can also have a global org cap to prevent runaway spend.
01:29 Evan: and during a traffic spike can you throttle gracefully, like allow some burst but drop or queue?
01:35 Samir: yes we support bursting with token buckets, and you can configure hard vs soft quotas. soft quotas will return warnings and optionally route to a cheaper model variant, hard quotas return 429s.
01:48 Priya: cheaper model variant routing — can that be automated per project?
01:52 Samir: yeah policy rules can be per-project, e.g., when latency under x ms or cost above y, fallback to quantized model or smaller model family. we'll show an example.
02:05 Alex: also worth noting we have rate-limit metrics per-token and per-request in the console so you can see budgets being consumed in near real-time.
02:15 Mark: ok show us the console.
02:22 Samir: switching to demo, pardon the screen share lag, here is the org overview, you can see Projects -> 'Aurora-PatientSearch', 'Aurora-Recommend', 'Aurora-Analytics'.
02:35 Samir: clicking into 'Aurora-PatientSearch' -> Keys tab, here you can create project keys, set scopes, and attach policies. policy editor supports conditions like time-of-day blocks, IP whitelists, and custom header enforcement.
03:05 Priya: can we limit by route? like allow embeddings for analytics but not for search?
03:12 Samir: yes you can whitelist endpoints per key, e.g., /v1/embeddings only for analytics key. we also support rate limiting per endpoint.
03:25 Janelle: audit logs — where do we store those and how long? retention?
03:30 Alex: audit logs are shipped to your configured SIEM or can be retained in the private console. default retention for org is 90 days, enterprise add-on supports longer retention and on-prem log sinks. logs include key id, requester, route, model, token counts.
03:48 Mark: ok what about SSO/SAML? we want role mapping to project-level permissions.
03:55 Lena: SSO via SAML/OIDC supported, role-based access in the console maps to org admin, project admin, project viewer etc. we can send a short RBAC mapping doc after.
04:06 Evan: on the networking side, if we deploy private, do rate-limits still enforce in the control plane or locally?
04:12 Samir: for private deployments we push a policy agent that enforces local limits and emits metrics; control plane can still coordinate but enforcement can be local for air-gapped scenarios.
04:24 Mark: great. show the policy example you mentioned.
04:29 Samir: here is a policy: project key 'PatientSearch' -> rate_limit: 100 reqs/min, token_quota: 10M/month, fallback: 'gpt-small-quant' when quota>80%. this policy also has an IP whitelist for our internal analytics cluster.
04:52 Priya: does the quota decrement on partial responses or per-token generation?
04:57 Samir: tokens are counted for both prompt and generation; we expose both token counts in response headers so you can aggregate. there is also a cache and batching layer — cached prefixes don't consume generation tokens when hit.
05:16 Janelle: is KMS key rotation supported? we need to rotate keys every 90 days and prove it for audits.
05:22 Alex: yes KMS integrations supported, rotations logged, and we provide an exportable proof-of-rotation report.
05:28 Mark: latency concerns — if we route to cheaper model during spike will that break quality for search?
05:34 Lena: that's a policy trade-off; you can set thresholds conservatively and route only non-critical traffic. also you can set per-route SLAs so critical endpoints never fallback.
05:44 Evan: do you support burst pooling across projects? sometimes product A isn't using its full budget and we want to let product B burst into unused capacity.
05:52 Samir: yes we have shared pools and priority buckets. you can configure project priorities and a shared reserve; when project A is underutilized its unused tokens can be borrowed by others up to configured limits.
06:08 Priya: sounds good. what's the visibility for cost attribution? we need per-product token cost back to our billing system.
06:14 Alex: Console exports per-project usage CSV with token counts, model used, timestamp, and cost estimate; we also support direct billing integrations via webhooks or invoice mapping.
06:26 Mark: any gotchas for HIPAA-ish data handling? we need data residency and encryption at rest in region.
06:33 Lena: for private deployments we can keep data in your VPC and region, encryption at rest with your KMS, and audit logs without leaving your network. for hosted we have region controls and BAA discussions.
06:45 Janelle: retention windows on logs again? 90 days by default, but we can push to your S3/GCS with custom retention.
06:53 Priya: demo time — can you show how to create a project key with a monthly quota and a hard limit?
06:58 Samir: sure, create -> name 'PatientSearch-prod' -> quota 10,000,000 tokens/month -> hard_limit true -> rate 50 reqs/sec. done. now the key page shows quota bar and alerts.
07:20 Mark: what happens when hard limit hits? 429s? any backoff hints returned?
07:25 Samir: 429 with Retry-After header, and optionally a structured JSON explaining quota exhausted and link to upgrade page. we also emit a usage alert to configured Slack or webhook.
07:40 Evan: can we set automated policy to spin up dedicated capacity when sustained usage exceeds x for y hours?
07:46 Alex: yes autoscale policies for dedicated pools exist; you can set thresholds that trigger on sustained QPS and provision extra capacity or burst to a reserved pool.
07:58 Mark: are rate limits enforced by token or request? we need to limit token-heavy requests as single reqs can be very large.
08:04 Samir: you can configure both. token-based rate limiting prevents few heavy requests from starving others; request-based is simpler but less granular.
08:18 Priya: ok, real question — we have multi-tenant customers inside our product, how do you recommend mapping tenants to projects or keys?
08:26 Samir: two patterns: 1) project-per-tenant for high isolation, 2) tenant-scoping within a project using sub-keys or claims for large scale. project-per-tenant gives clearer quotas but creates operational overhead at scale. we usually recommend project-per-product and tenant-level multiplexing with per-tenant quotas enforced at the app layer unless isolation is a compliance need.
08:52 Janelle: for regulated customers we might need project-per-tenant. can you automate key provisioning via API?
08:57 Lena: yes, key management APIs exist; you can programmatically create keys, rotate them, attach policies. we'll include API examples.
09:06 Mark: curious about throttling behavior during retries — will exponential backoff be honored?
09:10 Samir: we return standard 429 with Retry-After; clients should implement backoff. we also support a grace window to smooth retries to avoid thundering herds.
09:20 Priya: any plans to integrate org-level spend alerts?
09:23 Alex: yes org alerts and per-project alerts, thresholds with webhook/Slack/email.
09:28 Mark: ok what's the POC look like?
09:31 Lena: typical POC: 2 weeks, we give you a sandbox org with project keys, short-term dedicated pool if you want throughput tests, we run a small benchmark against your workload and produce a cost/latency report.
09:42 Priya: what do you need from us to start?
09:45 Lena: model list, expected QPS by route, example payload sizes, and which endpoints are critical vs best-effort.
09:52 Priya: we'll compile that and send.
09:56 Janelle: also security questionnaire, SOC2 and encryption docs.
10:00 Lena: we'll attach the security pack and SOC2 report in the follow-up.
10:04 Mark: ok let's do the POC. timeline – target kickoff 2025-03-10.
10:10 Lena: great. final recap: lena send pricing and sku, samir send policy diagram and api snippets, customer send model list and qps, schedule poc kickoff. thanks everyone.
10:25 Mark: thanks all.

Notes: transcription has a few small mishearings and brand names might be slightly off. References: shared deck link: https://redwood.ai/decks/rate-limits-org-keys (demo), security pack link: https://redwood.ai/security/small.pdf
